newsitem.title: USA: American Airlines cancels Fri intl flights.
newsitem.headline: American Airlines cancels Fri intl flights.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines said Thursday it was cancelling almost all of its Friday night international flights as it prepares for a possible pilots strike.

Spokesman Tim Smith said a total of 129 round-trips scheduled to leave on Friday Feb. 14 will be cancelled and that the only international flights set to go ahead as planned on Friday are 12 flights to London-Heathrow and two flights to London-Gatwick.
The return flights on Saturday Feb. 15 are also cancelled, he said.

"In light of the strike preparations, American has no choice but to minimize possible inconvenience to customers who would travel on certain flights, mainly long-haul international flights departing Friday Feb. 14," Smith said.
The announcement was made as airline management and pilots' union leaders continued to meet in Washington for last-ditch negotiations aimed at at staving off a strike.
The airline's announcement suggested it had little confidence in reaching a new four-year labor contract before the pilots' strike deadline of midnight Friday (0500 GMT).
Smith said American plans to reschedule its affected international passengers to Europe, the Far East and Latin America on earlier American flights or with other airlines.

He also said the airline was cancelling the flights "to comply with aircraft insurance requirements and in some cases because there is simply no parking space at certain congested international airports."

A pilots strike would entirely shut down American Airlines and its commuter carrier American Eagle. American is the second largest U.S. airline and carries about 200,000 passengers per day on 2,200 flights.
